ITEM PARAGRAPHS
The
bony
shell
of
a
sea
turtle
can
actually
sense
when
something
touches
it
.
A
series
of
thin
nerves
run
along
the
shell
and
detect
pressure
changes
associated
with
touch
.
The
nerves
do
not
contain
pain
receptors
so
scientists
do
not
think
sea
turtle
s
feel
pain
when
touched
on
the
shell
,
but
these
thin
nerves
could
transmit
information
to
other
parts
of
the
sea
turtle's
body
.
In
addition
,
researchers
and
scuba
divers
have
observed
sea
turtles
respond
to
the
stimulation
of
being
touched
on
the
skin
of
their
heads
and
their
flippers
.
